  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or

  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");

      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);

    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.

      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();

<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line ltx_leqno">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">On the largest prime factors of <math id="m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p-1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p+1</annotation></semantics></math></h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Genheng Zhao
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_address"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Address: </span>Academy of Mathematics and Systems Science, Chinese Academy of Sciences,
<br class="ltx_break">55 Zhongguancun East Road, Haidian District, Beijing 100190, China
</span>
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_email"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Email address: </span><a href="mailto:zhaogenheng@amss.ac.cn">zhaogenheng@amss.ac.cn</a>
</span></span></span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract.</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">We prove that each of the inequalities
<math id="abstract1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P^{+}(p+1)&gt;P^{+}(p-1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P^{+}(p+1)&gt;P^{+}(p-1)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="abstract1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P^{+}(p-1)&gt;P^{+}(p+1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P^{+}(p-1)&gt;P^{+}(p+1)</annotation></semantics></math> holds for a
positive proportion of primes. The argument combines a logarithmic
balance identity with a uniform Selberg sieve over a thin cofactor strip.
The same transfer mechanism applies to either shift and converts a
one-sided large-prime-factor reservoir into an unconditional ordering
result in both directions.</p>
  
</div>
<div class="ltx_keywords">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_keywords">Key words and phrases: </h6>largest prime factor, shifted primes, Selberg sieve, Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem
</div>
<div class="ltx_classification"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_classification">2020 Mathematics Subject Classification</h6>11N13, 11N35
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1. </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For <math id="S1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n&gt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n&gt;1</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="S1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P^{+}(n)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P^{+}(n)</annotation></semantics></math> denote its largest prime factor, and set
<math id="S1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P^{+}(1)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P^{+}(1)=1</annotation></semantics></math>. All logarithms are natural. We write</p>
<table id="S1.EGx1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S1.Ex1"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S1.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle G(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle G(x)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S1.Ex1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\#\{p\leq x:P^{+}(p+1)&gt;P^{+}(p-1)\}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>#</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\#\{p\leq x:P^{+}(p+1)&gt;P^{+}(p-1)\},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S1.Ex2"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S1.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\widetilde{G}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>G</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\widetilde{G}(x)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S1.Ex2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\#\{p\leq x:P^{+}(p-1)&gt;P^{+}(p+1)\}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>#</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\#\{p\leq x:P^{+}(p-1)&gt;P^{+}(p+1)\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> always denotes a prime.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The comparison of largest prime factors at neighbouring arguments has
a long history. The Erdős–Turán conjecture predicts that
<math id="S1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P^{+}(n)&lt;P^{+}(n+1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P^{+}(n)&lt;P^{+}(n+1)</annotation></semantics></math> holds for a set of integers of asymptotic density
<math id="S1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/2</annotation></semantics></math>. Erdős and Pomerance <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>]</cite> established a positive
lower density in 1978. Subsequent quantitative refinements include
the published bound <math id="S1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.2017" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.2017</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.2017</annotation></semantics></math> of Lü and Wang <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite>.
In a different direction, Teräväinen
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>, Theorem 1.16]</cite> proved that the logarithmic
density is <math id="S1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/2</annotation></semantics></math>, and Tao–Teräväinen
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>, Corollary 1.16]</cite> obtained the ordinary density <math id="S1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/2</annotation></semantics></math>
at all scales outside an exceptional set of logarithmic density zero.
Neither statement asserts the ordinary density limit at every scale.
These results concern an unrestricted integer variable; restricting
the middle argument to primes introduces an additional distribution
problem and does not follow by restriction of an integer-density
estimate. For the prime-variable ordering considered here,
Wang proved a positive-proportion result under the
Elliott–Halberstam conjecture <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite>; his survey
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite> discusses the prime-variable problem.
Our purpose is to obtain unconditional positive-proportion conclusions in
both directions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S1.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 1.1</span></span><span id="S1.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S1.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Each ordering occurs for a positive proportion of primes. More precisely,</span></p>
<table id="S1.Ex3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S1.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G(x)\gg\frac{x}{\log x},\qquad\widetilde{G}(x)\gg\frac{x}{\log x}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≫</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>G</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≫</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G(x)\gg\frac{x}{\log x},\qquad\widetilde{G}(x)\gg\frac{x}{\log x},</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="S1.Thmtheorem1.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.Thmtheorem1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">and hence</span></p>

</div>
<div id="S1.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_remark">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S1.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Remark 1.2</span></span><span id="S1.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></h6>
<div id="S1.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The proof permits a numerical positive lower coefficient, but we do not
calculate it here since it would be very tiny. For instance, the elementary reservoir estimate in
Proposition <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem3" title="Proposition 2.3. ‣ 2.2. One-sided reservoirs for both shifts ‣ 2. Logarithmic estimates and far reverse orderings ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a> permits
<math id="S1.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta=11/20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta=11/20</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta=1/4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta=1/4</annotation></semantics></math>; the remaining sieve and Euler-product
constants may be bounded coarsely. Our emphasis is the mechanism rather
than a small numerical value. No effective starting point is asserted,
since we use the classical Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The key feature is a transfer from one-sided large prime factors to a
comparison of two adjacent shifts. The one-sided problem has its own
classical development: Goldfeld <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite> obtained a
positive-proportion result for <math id="S1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P^{+}(p+a)&gt;x^{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>θ</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P^{+}(p+a)&gt;x^{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>, for fixed nonzero
<math id="S1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>, beyond <math id="S1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta=1/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta=1/2</annotation></semantics></math>, with exponent <math id="S1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.583\ldots" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.583</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.583\ldots</annotation></semantics></math>;
Baker and Harman <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>]</cite> later reached <math id="S1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.677" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.677</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.677</annotation></semantics></math>.
The formulation recorded by
Akbary–Hambrook <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>, Theorem 1.1]</cite> supplies, for any fixed
<math id="S1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/2&lt;\theta\leq 0.677" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>0.677</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/2&lt;\theta\leq 0.677</annotation></semantics></math>, a <math id="S1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> such that</p>
<table id="S1.Ex5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S1.Ex5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\#\{p\leq x:P^{+}(p+1)&gt;x^{\theta}\}\geq\delta\frac{x}{\log x}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>#</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>θ</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\#\{p\leq x:P^{+}(p+1)&gt;x^{\theta}\}\geq\delta\frac{x}{\log x}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S1.p3.2" class="ltx_p">for sufficiently large <math id="S1.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>. For the proof below, it is enough to obtain
the weaker choice <math id="S1.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta=11/20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta=11/20</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S1.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta=1/4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta=1/4</annotation></semantics></math> directly, as we do in
Proposition <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem3" title="Proposition 2.3. ‣ 2.2. One-sided reservoirs for both shifts ‣ 2. Logarithmic estimates and far reverse orderings ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a>.
Such a reservoir alone does not decide
which of <math id="S1.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P^{+}(p-1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P^{+}(p-1)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P^{+}(p+1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P^{+}(p+1)</annotation></semantics></math> is larger. We bridge that gap
by dividing the reverse orderings according to their distance from
the diagonal.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Write <math id="S1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q=P^{+}(p+1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q=P^{+}(p+1)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=P^{+}(p-1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=P^{+}(p-1)</annotation></semantics></math>. Within the reservoir
<math id="S1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q&gt;x^{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>θ</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q&gt;x^{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>, a balance identity for the logarithms above
<math id="S1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sqrt{x+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msqrt><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msqrt><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{x+1}</annotation></semantics></math> shows that a small number of desired
orderings forces a small number of reverse orderings with
<math id="S1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R&gt;x^{\eta}Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>η</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Q</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R&gt;x^{\eta}Q</annotation></semantics></math>, for any fixed <math id="S1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>.
This is an averaged constraint, not a pointwise relation between
<math id="S1.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math>. For the remaining reverse orderings, write
<math id="S1.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p+1=2aQ" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Q</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p+1=2aQ</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p-1=2bR" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p-1=2bR</annotation></semantics></math>. The ratio restriction confines the
cofactors to the thin multiplicative strip
<math id="S1.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b&lt;a\leq 2x^{\eta}b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>η</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b&lt;a\leq 2x^{\eta}b</annotation></semantics></math>. A three-linear-form upper-bound sieve, followed
by harmonic summation over this strip, gives</p>
<table id="S1.Ex6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S1.Ex6.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\#\{p\leq x:Q(p)&gt;x^{\theta},\ Q(p)&lt;R(p)\leq x^{\eta}Q(p)\}\ll_{\theta}\eta\frac{x}{\log x}+\frac{x}{\log^{2}x}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>#</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>θ</mi></msup><mo rspace="0.667em">,</mo><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>R</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>η</mi></msup><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><msub><mo>≪</mo><mi>θ</mi></msub><mi>η</mi><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\#\{p\leq x:Q(p)&gt;x^{\theta},\ Q(p)&lt;R(p)\leq x^{\eta}Q(p)\}\ll_{\theta}\eta\frac{x}{\log x}+\frac{x}{\log^{2}x}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S1.p4.2" class="ltx_p">The small factor <math id="S1.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math> is the decisive gain: summation over the
unrestricted cofactor box would lose it. The same argument works with
the roles of <math id="S1.p4.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p+1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.p4.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p-1</annotation></semantics></math> reversed. In that case the reservoir is
<math id="S1.p4.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R&gt;x^{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>θ</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R&gt;x^{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>, the undesired near-diagonal ordering is
<math id="S1.p4.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R&lt;Q\leq x^{\eta}R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>η</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R&lt;Q\leq x^{\eta}R</annotation></semantics></math>, and the cofactor relation <math id="S1.p4.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="aQ-bR=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Q</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">aQ-bR=1</annotation></semantics></math> forces
<math id="S1.p4.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a&lt;b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a&lt;b</annotation></semantics></math>; the identical uniform sieve then applies on the reflected thin
strip.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">A second feature is that the sieve estimate is uniform in cofactors
which grow with <math id="S1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>. We apply a classical Selberg upper-bound theorem
whose constants depend only on fixed local sieve conditions, and
verify those conditions and the remainder uniformly. Thus no
prime-tuple asymptotic or unverified dependence on growing coefficients
is needed. Combining the two controls and choosing a small fixed
<math id="S1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math> completes the transfer.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">For comparison, Yang’s recent preprint <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>, Theorem 1.6]</cite>
treats <math id="S1.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{y}^{+}(n)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>P</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{y}^{+}(n)</annotation></semantics></math>, the largest prime factor of <math id="S1.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> not exceeding <math id="S1.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>.
It gives a positive-proportion ordering result for shifted primes when
<math id="S1.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y=x^{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>α</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y=x^{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0&lt;\alpha&lt;17/32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mn>17</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0&lt;\alpha&lt;17/32</annotation></semantics></math>, which does not directly imply
the untruncated ordering considered here. Cofactor sieves also occur
in that work; the transfer above relies on their combination with
logarithmic balance and a thin strip.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Section <a href="#S2" title="2. Logarithmic estimates and far reverse orderings ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> establishes the logarithmic estimates and
the far-from-diagonal bounds in both directions. Section <a href="#S3" title="3. A uniform sieve over a thin cofactor strip ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>
treats the two reflected near-diagonal sets by the same uniform sieve
and thin-strip summation. Section <a href="#S4" title="4. Completion of the argument ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> closes both arguments. All external analytic
inputs are classical published results.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2. </span>Logarithmic estimates and far reverse orderings</h2>

<section id="S2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.1. </span>The balance identity</h3>

<div id="S2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For primes <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\leq x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\leq x</annotation></semantics></math>, write</p>
<table id="S2.Ex7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q(p)=P^{+}(p+1),\quad R(p)=P^{+}(p-1),\quad Z=\sqrt{x+1}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q(p)=P^{+}(p+1),\quad R(p)=P^{+}(p-1),\quad Z=\sqrt{x+1},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">and define</p>
<table id="S2.Ex8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{-}(p)=\mathbf{1}_{R(p)&gt;Z}\log R(p),\qquad L_{+}(p)=\mathbf{1}_{Q(p)&gt;Z}\log Q(p)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mn>𝟏</mn><mrow><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mo>+</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mn>𝟏</mn><mrow><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{-}(p)=\mathbf{1}_{R(p)&gt;Z}\log R(p),\qquad L_{+}(p)=\mathbf{1}_{Q(p)&gt;Z}\log Q(p).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S2.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 2.1</span></span><span id="S2.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">As <math id="S2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="S2.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(1)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{p\leq x}\bigl(L_{-}(p)-L_{+}(p)\bigr)=o(x)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mo lspace="0em" maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mo>+</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{p\leq x}\bigl(L_{-}(p)-L_{+}(p)\bigr)=o(x).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.Thmtheorem1.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.Thmtheorem1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">In fact the proof gives <math id="S2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(x\log\log x/\log x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>log</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(x\log\log x/\log x)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS1.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S2.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Lambda</annotation></semantics></math> be the von Mangoldt function and let <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(x;d,c)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(x;d,c)</annotation></semantics></math> count
primes at most <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> congruent to <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> modulo <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>.
Since <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log n=\sum_{d\mid n}\Lambda(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log n=\sum_{d\mid n}\Lambda(d)</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="S2.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(2)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{3\leq p\leq x}\log\frac{p-1}{p+1}=\sum_{d\leq x+1}\Lambda(d)\bigl(\pi(x;d,1)-\pi(x;d,-1)\bigr)+\log 3." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></munder><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{3\leq p\leq x}\log\frac{p-1}{p+1}=\sum_{d\leq x+1}\Lambda(d)\bigl(\pi(x;d,1)-\pi(x;d,-1)\bigr)+\log 3.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS1.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">This is exact for <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\geq 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\geq 3</annotation></semantics></math>: the only correction is removal of <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=2</annotation></semantics></math>,
whose contribution is <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-\log 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">−</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\log 3</annotation></semantics></math>. There is no discrepancy at <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=x+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=x+1</annotation></semantics></math>.
The left side is <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\log\log x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(\log\log x)</annotation></semantics></math> because
<math id="S2.SS1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\log((p-1)/(p+1))|\ll 1/p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≪</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\log((p-1)/(p+1))|\ll 1/p</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">Apply the classical Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem in its maximal
<math id="S2.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\psi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ψ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\psi</annotation></semantics></math>-form, as recorded in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>, Introduction]</cite>, with saving
exponent <math id="S2.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A=3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A=3</annotation></semantics></math>. Choose its associated fixed <math id="S2.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>, enlarge it to
<math id="S2.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B\geq 6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B\geq 6</annotation></semantics></math>, and put <math id="S2.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D=x^{1/2}/(\log x)^{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>/</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>B</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D=x^{1/2}/(\log x)^{B}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Here <math id="S2.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\psi(t;d,c)=\sum_{n\leq t,\ n\equiv c\pmod{d}}\Lambda(n)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ψ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.577em">,</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≡</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mspace style="width:0.949em;" width="0.949em"></mspace><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">mod</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\psi(t;d,c)=\sum_{n\leq t,\ n\equiv c\pmod{d}}\Lambda(n)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Thus</span></p>
<table id="S2.Ex9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{d\leq D}\max_{(c,d)=1}\max_{2\leq t\leq x}\left|\psi(t;d,c)-\frac{t}{\varphi(d)}\right|\ll\frac{x}{\log^{3}x}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mrow><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munder><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></munder></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ψ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>φ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≪</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{d\leq D}\max_{(c,d)=1}\max_{2\leq t\leq x}\left|\psi(t;d,c)-\frac{t}{\varphi(d)}\right|\ll\frac{x}{\log^{3}x}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS1.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">Removing prime powers costs at most <math id="S2.SS1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\sqrt{x}\log^{2}x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(\sqrt{x}\log^{2}x)</annotation></semantics></math> per modulus,
uniformly for <math id="S2.SS1.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\leq x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\leq x</annotation></semantics></math>. Partial summation against <math id="S2.SS1.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/\log t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/\log t</annotation></semantics></math>
then gives the <math id="S2.SS1.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>-form below: its kernel has bounded total
variation on <math id="S2.SS1.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[2,x]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[2,x]</annotation></semantics></math>, and the summed prime-power and lower-endpoint
errors are <math id="S2.SS1.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(D\sqrt{x}\log^{2}x+D)\ll x/\log^{4}x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≪</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(D\sqrt{x}\log^{2}x+D)\ll x/\log^{4}x</annotation></semantics></math>.
Consequently</span></p>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{d\leq D}\max_{(c,d)=1}\left|\pi(x;d,c)-\frac{\operatorname{Li}(x)}{\varphi(d)}\right|\ll\frac{x}{\log^{3}x}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munder><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>Li</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>φ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≪</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{d\leq D}\max_{(c,d)=1}\left|\pi(x;d,c)-\frac{\operatorname{Li}(x)}{\varphi(d)}\right|\ll\frac{x}{\log^{3}x}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="S2.SS1.p3.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS1.p3.3.1" class="ltx_text">The main terms in the two reduced classes <math id="S2.SS1.p3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1,-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1,-1</annotation></semantics></math> cancel, giving</span></p>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left|\sum_{d\leq D}\Lambda(d)\bigl(\pi(x;d,1)-\pi(x;d,-1)\bigr)\right|\ll\frac{x}{\log^{2}x}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><munder><mo lspace="0em" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>≪</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|\sum_{d\leq D}\Lambda(d)\bigl(\pi(x;d,1)-\pi(x;d,-1)\bigr)\right|\ll\frac{x}{\log^{2}x}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<div id="S2.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">For <math id="S2.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D&lt;d\leq Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D&lt;d\leq Z</annotation></semantics></math>, Brun–Titchmarsh
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>, Lemma 3.1(f), equation (3.11)]</cite> gives</span></p>
<table id="S2.Ex11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(x;d,\pm 1)\ll\frac{x}{\varphi(d)\log(x/d)}\ll\frac{x}{\varphi(d)\log x}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≪</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>φ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>≪</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>φ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(x;d,\pm 1)\ll\frac{x}{\varphi(d)\log(x/d)}\ll\frac{x}{\varphi(d)\log x}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.p4.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS1.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text">The constants are uniform since <math id="S2.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d\leq\sqrt{x+1}&lt;x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>≤</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\leq\sqrt{x+1}&lt;x</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="S2.SS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log(x/d)\geq(1/2+o(1))\log x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log(x/d)\geq(1/2+o(1))\log x</annotation></semantics></math>.
We shall use</span></p>
<table id="S2.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(4)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{n\leq y}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{\varphi(n)}=\log y+O(1)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>φ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{n\leq y}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{\varphi(n)}=\log y+O(1).</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="S2.SS1.p4.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS1.p4.3.1" class="ltx_text">Indeed, the classical estimate
<math id="S2.SS1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{n\leq y}\Lambda(n)/n=\log y+O(1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{n\leq y}\Lambda(n)/n=\log y+O(1)</annotation></semantics></math> implies this because</span></p>

<p id="S2.SS1.p4.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS1.p4.4.1" class="ltx_text">Subtracting (<a href="#S2.E4" title="In Proof. ‣ 2.1. The balance identity ‣ 2. Logarithmic estimates and far reverse orderings ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>) at <math id="S2.SS1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.SS1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> therefore yields</span></p>

<div id="S2.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text">An integer at most <math id="S2.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x+1</annotation></semantics></math> has at most one prime divisor greater than <math id="S2.SS1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math>,
and that divisor cannot occur to the second power. Thus the terms <math id="S2.SS1.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=q&gt;Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=q&gt;Z</annotation></semantics></math>
in (<a href="#S2.E2" title="In Proof. ‣ 2.1. The balance identity ‣ 2. Logarithmic estimates and far reverse orderings ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>) give exactly <math id="S2.SS1.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{-}(p)-L_{+}(p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mo>+</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{-}(p)-L_{+}(p)</annotation></semantics></math>.
The remaining terms <math id="S2.SS1.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=q^{k}&gt;Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=q^{k}&gt;Z</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.SS1.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math>, are bounded in absolute value
by a prime-power error <math id="S2.SS1.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{\rm pp}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>pp</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{\rm pp}</annotation></semantics></math>. Each class modulo <math id="S2.SS1.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{k}</annotation></semantics></math> contains
at most <math id="S2.SS1.p5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x/q^{k}+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x/q^{k}+1</annotation></semantics></math> positive integers at most <math id="S2.SS1.p5.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, so</span></p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{\rm pp}\ll\sum_{2\leq k\leq K}\ \sum_{Z&lt;q^{k}\leq x+1}\log q\left(\frac{x}{q^{k}}+1\right),\qquad K=\left\lfloor\frac{\log(x+1)}{\log 2}\right\rfloor." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>pp</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">≪</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><msup><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></munder><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>x</mi><msup><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msup></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>⌊</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>⌋</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{\rm pp}\ll\sum_{2\leq k\leq K}\ \sum_{Z&lt;q^{k}\leq x+1}\log q\left(\frac{x}{q^{k}}+1\right),\qquad K=\left\lfloor\frac{\log(x+1)}{\log 2}\right\rfloor.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="S2.SS1.p5.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS1.p5.2.1" class="ltx_text">For <math id="S2.SS1.p5.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=2</annotation></semantics></math>, Chebyshev’s bound <math id="S2.SS1.p5.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{q\leq t}\log q\ll t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>≪</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{q\leq t}\log q\ll t</annotation></semantics></math> and partial
summation give</span></p>

<p id="S2.SS1.p5.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS1.p5.3.1" class="ltx_text">For <math id="S2.SS1.p5.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\geq 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\geq 3</annotation></semantics></math>, put <math id="S2.SS1.p5.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{k}=(x+1)^{1/(2k)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{k}=(x+1)^{1/(2k)}</annotation></semantics></math>. Uniformly for real <math id="S2.SS1.p5.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math>
and integers <math id="S2.SS1.p5.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="S2.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(6)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{n&gt;y}\frac{\log n}{n^{k}}\ll y^{1-k}\log(2y)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><msup><mi>n</mi><mi>k</mi></msup></mfrac></mrow><mo>≪</mo><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{n&gt;y}\frac{\log n}{n^{k}}\ll y^{1-k}\log(2y).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
