</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.p5.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS1.p5.4.1" class="ltx_text">For completeness, split the integers into <math id="S2.SS1.p5.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2^{j}y&lt;n\leq 2^{j+1}y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>j</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^{j}y&lt;n\leq 2^{j+1}y</annotation></semantics></math>.
The contribution of the <math id="S2.SS1.p5.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>th block is at most an absolute constant times
<math id="S2.SS1.p5.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y^{1-k}2^{-j(k-1)}(\log(2y)+(j+1)\log 2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{1-k}2^{-j(k-1)}(\log(2y)+(j+1)\log 2)</annotation></semantics></math>; summing the geometric
series proves (<a href="#S2.E6" title="In Proof. ‣ 2.1. The balance identity ‣ 2. Logarithmic estimates and far reverse orderings ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>) with a constant independent of <math id="S2.SS1.p5.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>.
It follows that the <math id="S2.SS1.p5.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>th contribution is</span></p>
<table id="S2.Ex15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ll x^{1/2+1/(2k)}\log x+(x+1)^{1/k}\ll x^{2/3}\log x+x^{1/3}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≪</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>≪</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ll x^{1/2+1/(2k)}\log x+(x+1)^{1/k}\ll x^{2/3}\log x+x^{1/3}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.p5.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS1.p5.5.1" class="ltx_text">There are <math id="S2.SS1.p5.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\log x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(\log x)</annotation></semantics></math> such <math id="S2.SS1.p5.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>, whence</span></p>
<table id="S2.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(7)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{\rm pp}\ll x^{3/4}+x^{2/3}\log^{2}x=o(x)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>pp</mi></msub><mo>≪</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{\rm pp}\ll x^{3/4}+x^{2/3}\log^{2}x=o(x).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.p5.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS1.p5.6.1" class="ltx_text">Combining (<a href="#S2.E2" title="In Proof. ‣ 2.1. The balance identity ‣ 2. Logarithmic estimates and far reverse orderings ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>), (<a href="#S2.E3" title="In Proof. ‣ 2.1. The balance identity ‣ 2. Logarithmic estimates and far reverse orderings ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>), (<a href="#S2.E5" title="In Proof. ‣ 2.1. The balance identity ‣ 2. Logarithmic estimates and far reverse orderings ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>)
and (<a href="#S2.E7" title="In Proof. ‣ 2.1. The balance identity ‣ 2. Logarithmic estimates and far reverse orderings ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>) proves the lemma. Restoring <math id="S2.SS1.p5.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=2</annotation></semantics></math> costs only <math id="S2.SS1.p5.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(1)</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.2. </span>One-sided reservoirs for both shifts</h3>

<div id="S2.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S2.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 2.2</span></span><span id="S2.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For either sign <math id="S2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s\in\{-1,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s\in\{-1,1\}</annotation></semantics></math>, as <math id="S2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="S2.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(8)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{p\leq x}\mathbf{1}_{P^{+}(p+s)&gt;Z}\log P^{+}(p+s)=\frac{x}{2}+O\!\left(\frac{x\log\log x}{\log x}\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><msub><mn>𝟏</mn><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.621em;" width="0.621em"><mi>O</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>log</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{p\leq x}\mathbf{1}_{P^{+}(p+s)&gt;Z}\log P^{+}(p+s)=\frac{x}{2}+O\!\left(\frac{x\log\log x}{\log x}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.Thmtheorem2.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.Thmtheorem2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For <math id="S2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s=-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s=-1</annotation></semantics></math>, the term <math id="S2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=2</annotation></semantics></math> is understood as zero.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">The proof of Lemma <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem1" title="Lemma 2.1. ‣ 2.1. The balance identity ‣ 2. Logarithmic estimates and far reverse orderings ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a> also estimates each small-divisor
sum separately. For <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D=x^{1/2}/\log^{B}x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>/</mo><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mi>B</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D=x^{1/2}/\log^{B}x</annotation></semantics></math>, its small-modulus part is</span></p>
<table id="S2.EGx2" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S2.Ex16"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S2.Ex16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\sum_{d\leq D}\Lambda(d)\pi(x;d,-s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></munder></mstyle><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\sum_{d\leq D}\Lambda(d)\pi(x;d,-s)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S2.Ex16.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\operatorname{Li}(x)\sum_{d\leq D}\frac{\Lambda(d)}{\varphi(d)}+O(x/\log^{2}x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Li</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></munder></mstyle><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>φ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\operatorname{Li}(x)\sum_{d\leq D}\frac{\Lambda(d)}{\varphi(d)}+O(x/\log^{2}x)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S2.Ex17"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>

</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text">The part <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D&lt;d\leq Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D&lt;d\leq Z</annotation></semantics></math> is bounded by (<a href="#S2.E5" title="In Proof. ‣ 2.1. The balance identity ‣ 2. Logarithmic estimates and far reverse orderings ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>).
The quantitative prime number theorem in the form
<math id="S2.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\vartheta(t)=\sum_{p\leq t}\log p=t+O(t/\log t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ϑ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\vartheta(t)=\sum_{p\leq t}\log p=t+O(t/\log t)</annotation></semantics></math>
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>, Lemma 3.1(d)]</cite> gives
<math id="S2.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{3\leq p\leq x}\log(p+s)=x+O(x/\log x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{3\leq p\leq x}\log(p+s)=x+O(x/\log x)</annotation></semantics></math>: replacing
<math id="S2.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log(p+s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log(p+s)</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log p</annotation></semantics></math> costs <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\log\log x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(\log\log x)</annotation></semantics></math>.
The prime-power discrepancy above <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math> is bounded by (<a href="#S2.E7" title="In Proof. ‣ 2.1. The balance identity ‣ 2. Logarithmic estimates and far reverse orderings ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>).
Subtracting the small-divisor sum from the total logarithmic mass
therefore gives (<a href="#S2.E8" title="In Lemma 2.2. ‣ 2.2. One-sided reservoirs for both shifts ‣ 2. Logarithmic estimates and far reverse orderings ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>). The <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=2</annotation></semantics></math> endpoint costs <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(1)</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S2.Thmtheorem3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 2.3</span></span><span id="S2.Thmtheorem3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For <math id="S2.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/2&lt;\beta&lt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/2&lt;\beta&lt;1</annotation></semantics></math>, put</span></p>
<table id="S2.Ex19" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta(\beta)=\frac{1}{2}+2\log(2-2\beta)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta(\beta)=\frac{1}{2}+2\log(2-2\beta).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.Thmtheorem3.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.Thmtheorem3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Then, for either sign <math id="S2.Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s\in\{-1,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s\in\{-1,1\}</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="S2.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(9)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\liminf_{x\to\infty}\frac{\log x}{x}\#\{p\leq x:P^{+}(p+s)&gt;x^{\beta}\}\geq\Delta(\beta)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim inf</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mi>x</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>#</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>β</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\liminf_{x\to\infty}\frac{\log x}{x}\#\{p\leq x:P^{+}(p+s)&gt;x^{\beta}\}\geq\Delta(\beta).</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="S2.Thmtheorem3.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.Thmtheorem3.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">In particular this coefficient is positive for
<math id="S2.Thmtheorem3.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\beta&lt;1-\tfrac{1}{2}e^{-1/4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>e</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta&lt;1-\tfrac{1}{2}e^{-1/4}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>

<div id="S2.SS2.3" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Fix <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s\in\{-1,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s\in\{-1,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta&gt;1/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta&gt;1/2</annotation></semantics></math>. Eventually <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{\beta}&gt;Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>β</mi></msup><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{\beta}&gt;Z</annotation></semantics></math>.
At most one prime factor of <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p+s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p+s</annotation></semantics></math> exceeds <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math>, so, apart from the
harmless endpoint <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=2</annotation></semantics></math> when <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s=-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s=-1</annotation></semantics></math>, the logarithmic mass removed
between <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{\beta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>β</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{\beta}</annotation></semantics></math> is exactly</span></p>
<table id="S2.Ex20" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{s}(x;\beta)=\sum_{Z&lt;q\leq x^{\beta}}(\log q)\pi(x;q,-s)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>≤</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>β</mi></msup></mrow></munder><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{s}(x;\beta)=\sum_{Z&lt;q\leq x^{\beta}}(\log q)\pi(x;q,-s).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS2.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">Brun–Titchmarsh <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>, Lemma 3.1(f), equation (3.11)]</cite>
bounds this uniformly in the sign by</span></p>
<table id="S2.Ex21" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex21.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2x\sum_{Z&lt;q\leq x^{\beta}}\frac{\log q}{(q-1)\log(x/q)}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>≤</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>β</mi></msup></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x\sum_{Z&lt;q\leq x^{\beta}}\frac{\log q}{(q-1)\log(x/q)}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.p2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS2.p2.3.1" class="ltx_text">Replacing <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q-1</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> changes this bound by <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{\beta}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>β</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{\beta}(x)</annotation></semantics></math>,
since <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log(x/q)\geq(1-\beta)\log x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log(x/q)\geq(1-\beta)\log x</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="S2.SS2.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{q&gt;Z}\log q/q^{2}\ll 1/Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>q</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>≪</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{q&gt;Z}\log q/q^{2}\ll 1/Z</annotation></semantics></math>.
Use the Mertens estimate <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A(t)=\sum_{q\leq t}\log q/q=\log t+O(1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A(t)=\sum_{q\leq t}\log q/q=\log t+O(1)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Partial summation against <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/\log(x/t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/\log(x/t)</annotation></semantics></math> gives</span></p>
<table id="S2.EGx3" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S2.Ex22"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S2.Ex22.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\sum_{Z&lt;q\leq x^{\beta}}\frac{\log q}{q\log(x/q)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>≤</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>β</mi></msup></mrow></munder></mstyle><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\sum_{Z&lt;q\leq x^{\beta}}\frac{\log q}{q\log(x/q)}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S2.Ex22.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\int_{Z}^{x^{\beta}}\frac{dt}{t\log(x/t)}+O_{\beta}(1/\log x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><mi>Z</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>β</mi></msup></msubsup></mstyle><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>O</mi><mi>β</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\int_{Z}^{x^{\beta}}\frac{dt}{t\log(x/t)}+O_{\beta}(1/\log x)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S2.Ex23"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S2.Ex23.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\log\frac{\log(x/Z)}{(1-\beta)\log x}+O_{\beta}(1/\log x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>O</mi><mi>β</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\log\frac{\log(x/Z)}{(1-\beta)\log x}+O_{\beta}(1/\log x)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S2.Ex24"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S2.Ex24.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=-\log(2-2\beta)+o_{\beta}(1)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">−</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>β</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=-\log(2-2\beta)+o_{\beta}(1).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.p2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS2.p2.4.1" class="ltx_text">The partial summation error follows because the endpoint values and
the total variation of <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/\log(x/t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/\log(x/t)</annotation></semantics></math> on this interval are
<math id="S2.SS2.p2.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O_{\beta}(1/\log x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>O</mi><mi>β</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O_{\beta}(1/\log x)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Lemma <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem2" title="Lemma 2.2. ‣ 2.2. One-sided reservoirs for both shifts ‣ 2. Logarithmic estimates and far reverse orderings ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a> now implies, uniformly for the fixed sign <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="S2.Ex25" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex25.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}p\leq x\\
P^{+}(p+s)&gt;x^{\beta}\end{subarray}}\log P^{+}(p+s)\geq\Delta(\beta)x+o_{\beta}(x)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mtable rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>β</mi></msup></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></munder><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>β</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}p\leq x\\
P^{+}(p+s)&gt;x^{\beta}\end{subarray}}\log P^{+}(p+s)\geq\Delta(\beta)x+o_{\beta}(x).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.p2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS2.p2.5.1" class="ltx_text">Each logarithm is at most <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log(x+1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log(x+1)</annotation></semantics></math>, proving
(<a href="#S2.E9" title="In Proposition 2.3. ‣ 2.2. One-sided reservoirs for both shifts ‣ 2. Logarithmic estimates and far reverse orderings ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>). If <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta(\beta)\leq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta(\beta)\leq 0</annotation></semantics></math>, the resulting
lower bound is simply vacuous.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_remark">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S2.Thmtheorem4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Remark 2.4</span></span><span id="S2.Thmtheorem4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></h6>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.Thmtheorem4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">See <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>, Theorem 2.5]</cite> for the same expression <math id="S2.Thmtheorem4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> in the
quantitative minus-shift setting. The argument above treats both signs
directly using standard published inputs: Bombieri–Vinogradov,
Brun–Titchmarsh, Mertens’ theorem, and the prime number theorem.
An explicit density coefficient does not give an effective starting
point, since the BV estimate used in Lemma <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem2" title="Lemma 2.2. ‣ 2.2. One-sided reservoirs for both shifts ‣ 2. Logarithmic estimates and far reverse orderings ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a> is ineffective.</p>
</div>
</div>
</section>

<div id="S2.Thmtheorem5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S2.Thmtheorem5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 2.5</span></span><span id="S2.Thmtheorem5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.Thmtheorem5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.Thmtheorem5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For every fixed <math id="S2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="S2.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(10)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\#\mathcal{F}_{\eta}(x)\leq\frac{G(x)}{\eta}+o_{\eta}\!\left(\frac{x}{\log x}\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>#</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi>η</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>η</mi></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>η</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\#\mathcal{F}_{\eta}(x)\leq\frac{G(x)}{\eta}+o_{\eta}\!\left(\frac{x}{\log x}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>

</div>

<div id="S2.SS3.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S2.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">For sufficiently large <math id="S2.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{\theta}&gt;Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>θ</mi></msup><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{\theta}&gt;Z</annotation></semantics></math>. Every prime in
<math id="S2.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{F}_{\eta}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi>η</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{F}_{\eta}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> contributes to the balance sum an amount</span></p>
<table id="S2.Ex28" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex28.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log\frac{R(p)}{Q(p)}&gt;\eta\log x." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log\frac{R(p)}{Q(p)}&gt;\eta\log x.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS3.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS3.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">The truncated logarithm is nondecreasing for <math id="S2.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math>.
Hence primes with <math id="S2.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q(p)\leq R(p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q(p)\leq R(p)</annotation></semantics></math> contribute nonnegatively, and only
primes counted by <math id="S2.SS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G(x)</annotation></semantics></math> can contribute negatively, by at most
<math id="S2.SS3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log(x+1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log(x+1)</annotation></semantics></math> each. Therefore</span></p>
<table id="S2.Ex29" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex29.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta\log x\,\#\mathcal{F}_{\eta}(x)\leq G(x)\log(x+1)+o(x)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>#</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi>η</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta\log x\,\#\mathcal{F}_{\eta}(x)\leq G(x)\log(x+1)+o(x).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS3.p2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS3.p2.3.1" class="ltx_text">After division, replacing <math id="S2.SS3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log(x+1)/\log x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log(x+1)/\log x</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="S2.SS3.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> costs
<math id="S2.SS3.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(1/\log x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(1/\log x)</annotation></semantics></math>, even using the trivial <math id="S2.SS3.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G(x)\leq x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G(x)\leq x</annotation></semantics></math>.
This proves (<a href="#S2.E10" title="In Lemma 2.5. ‣ 2.3. Orderings far from the diagonal ‣ 2. Logarithmic estimates and far reverse orderings ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>); the error is for fixed <math id="S2.SS3.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math>, as required.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">

<div id="S2.Thmtheorem6" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S2.Thmtheorem6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 2.6</span></span><span id="S2.Thmtheorem6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>

<p id="S2.Thmtheorem6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.Thmtheorem6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For every fixed <math id="S2.Thmtheorem6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>

<div id="S2.SS3.3" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S2.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">Apply the balance identity with the sign reversed. Every prime in
<math id="S2.SS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{\mathcal{F}}_{\eta}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>η</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{\mathcal{F}}_{\eta}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> contributes to
<math id="S2.SS3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{+}(p)-L_{-}(p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mo>+</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{+}(p)-L_{-}(p)</annotation></semantics></math> an amount</span></p>
<table id="S2.Ex31" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex31.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log\frac{Q(p)}{R(p)}&gt;\eta\log x." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log\frac{Q(p)}{R(p)}&gt;\eta\log x.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS3.p4.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS3.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text">Primes with <math id="S2.SS3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R(p)\leq Q(p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R(p)\leq Q(p)</annotation></semantics></math> contribute nonnegatively to this reversed
balance sum, while only primes counted by <math id="S2.SS3.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{G}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>G</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{G}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> can
contribute negatively, and each such contribution has absolute value
at most <math id="S2.SS3.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log(x+1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log(x+1)</annotation></semantics></math>. Hence</span></p>
<table id="S2.Ex32" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex32.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta\log x\,\#\widetilde{\mathcal{F}}_{\eta}(x)\leq\widetilde{G}(x)\log(x+1)+o(x)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>#</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>η</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>G</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta\log x\,\#\widetilde{\mathcal{F}}_{\eta}(x)\leq\widetilde{G}(x)\log(x+1)+o(x),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS3.p4.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.SS3.p4.3.1" class="ltx_text">which gives (<a href="#S2.E11" title="In Lemma 2.6. ‣ 2.3. Orderings far from the diagonal ‣ 2. Logarithmic estimates and far reverse orderings ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>) exactly as in
Lemma <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem5" title="Lemma 2.5. ‣ 2.3. Orderings far from the diagonal ‣ 2. Logarithmic estimates and far reverse orderings ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.5</span></a>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3. </span>A uniform sieve over a thin cofactor strip</h2>

<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1. </span>Cofactors and local densities</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Put</p>
<table id="S3.Ex33" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex33.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{N}_{\eta}(x)=\{p\in\mathcal{A}_{\theta}(x):Q(p)&lt;R(p)\leq x^{\eta}Q(p)\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mi>η</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo rspace="0.278em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>η</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{N}_{\eta}(x)=\{p\in\mathcal{A}_{\theta}(x):Q(p)&lt;R(p)\leq x^{\eta}Q(p)\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">For later use in the opposite direction also put</p>
<table id="S3.Ex34" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex34.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}_{\eta}(x)=\{p\in\widetilde{\mathcal{A}}_{\theta}(x):R(p)&lt;Q(p)\leq x^{\eta}R(p)\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>η</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo rspace="0.278em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>η</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>R</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}_{\eta}(x)=\{p\in\widetilde{\mathcal{A}}_{\theta}(x):R(p)&lt;Q(p)\leq x^{\eta}R(p)\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">For <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in\mathcal{N}_{\eta}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mi>η</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\in\mathcal{N}_{\eta}(x)</annotation></semantics></math>, write <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q=Q(p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q=Q(p)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=R(p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=R(p)</annotation></semantics></math>. Since
<math id="S3.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q,r&gt;x^{\theta}&gt;3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>θ</mi></msup><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q,r&gt;x^{\theta}&gt;3</annotation></semantics></math>, these factors are odd and we can write uniquely</p>
<table id="S3.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(12)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p+1=2aq,\qquad p-1=2br,\qquad aq-br=1." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p+1=2aq,\qquad p-1=2br,\qquad aq-br=1.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.4" class="ltx_p">Consequently <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a,b)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a,b)=1</annotation></semantics></math>, and for <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math> the explicit bounds are</p>

<p id="S3.SS1.p1.6" class="ltx_p">Thus, for sufficiently large <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> depending only on <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>

<p id="S3.SS1.p1.7" class="ltx_p">One of <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p-1,p+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p-1,p+1</annotation></semantics></math> is divisible by <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math> and one by <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q,r&gt;3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q,r&gt;3</annotation></semantics></math>,
the remaining factors <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2,3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2,3</annotation></semantics></math> occur in <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6\mid ab" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6\mid ab</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">Fix a coprime pair satisfying <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6\mid ab" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6\mid ab</annotation></semantics></math> and (<a href="#S3.E13" title="In 3.1. <p id="S3.SS1.p2.4" class="ltx_p">For triples from (<a href="#S3.E12" title="In 3.1. Cofactors and local densities ‣ 3. All intercepts are nonnegative integers, and leading coefficients are
positive.
