<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(17)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H(n)=\prod_{\begin{subarray}{c}\ell&gt;3\\
\ell\mid n\end{subarray}}\frac{\ell-1}{\ell-3}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∏</mo><mtable rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></munder><mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(n)=\prod_{\begin{subarray}{c}\ell&gt;3\\
\ell\mid n\end{subarray}}\frac{\ell-1}{\ell-3}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 3.1</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Primitive forms and local densities)<span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The three forms are primitive and pairwise nonproportional.
For the number <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(\ell)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho(\ell)</annotation></semantics></math> of roots of <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{1}L_{2}L_{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{1}L_{2}L_{3}</annotation></semantics></math> modulo <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="S3.E18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(18)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(2)=\rho(3)=1,\qquad\rho(\ell)=\begin{cases}3,&amp;\ell&gt;3,\ \ell\nmid ab,\\
1,&amp;\ell&gt;3,\ \ell\mid ab.\end{cases}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>3</mn><mo rspace="0.667em">,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>∤</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.667em">,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho(2)=\rho(3)=1,\qquad\rho(\ell)=\begin{cases}3,&amp;\ell&gt;3,\ \ell\nmid ab,\\
1,&amp;\ell&gt;3,\ \ell\mid ab.\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">In particular <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0&lt;\rho(\ell)&lt;\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0&lt;\rho(\ell)&lt;\ell</annotation></semantics></math> at every prime, and</span></p>
<table id="S3.E19" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(19)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{S}(a,b)=\prod_{\ell}(1-\rho(\ell)/\ell)(1-1/\ell)^{-3}=C_{3}H(ab)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔖</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∏</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></munder><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{S}(a,b)=\prod_{\ell}(1-\rho(\ell)/\ell)(1-1/\ell)^{-3}=C_{3}H(ab),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{3}=9\prod_{\ell&gt;3}(1-3/\ell)(1-1/\ell)^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0em">∏</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{3}=9\prod_{\ell&gt;3}(1-3/\ell)(1-1/\ell)^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math> is an
absolutely convergent positive constant.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S3.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">The defining congruences give <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(2ab,n_{0})=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2ab,n_{0})=1</annotation></semantics></math>. If an odd prime divided
both <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{0}\equiv 1\pmod{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>≡</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mspace style="width:0.949em;" width="0.949em"></mspace><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">mod</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{0}\equiv 1\pmod{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="S3.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{0}+1\equiv 0\pmod{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>≡</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mspace style="width:0.949em;" width="0.949em"></mspace><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">mod</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{0}+1\equiv 0\pmod{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>, an impossibility. If <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\mid b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\mid b</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="S3.SS1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> is odd and <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{0}\equiv 1\pmod{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>≡</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mspace style="width:0.949em;" width="0.949em"></mspace><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">mod</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{0}\equiv 1\pmod{4}</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(n_{0}+1)/(2a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(n_{0}+1)/(2a)</annotation></semantics></math> is odd.
Thus <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(b,B_{1})=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(b,B_{1})=1</annotation></semantics></math>. Similarly <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a,B_{3})=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a,B_{3})=1</annotation></semantics></math>: when <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\mid a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\mid a</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="S3.SS1.p3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> is odd and <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{0}\equiv-1\pmod{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>≡</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mspace style="width:0.949em;" width="0.949em"></mspace><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">mod</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{0}\equiv-1\pmod{4}</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{3}</annotation></semantics></math> is odd.
The nonzero determinants establish nonproportionality.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">If <math id="S3.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell&gt;3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell&gt;3</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell\nmid ab" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>∤</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell\nmid ab</annotation></semantics></math>, all three coefficients are invertible
and (<a href="#S3.E16" title="In 3.1. Cofactors and local densities ‣ 3. A uniform sieve over a thin cofactor strip ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">16</span></a>) gives three distinct roots. If an odd <math id="S3.SS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell\mid a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell\mid a</annotation></semantics></math>,
then <math id="S3.SS1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell\nmid b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>∤</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell\nmid b</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{2}\equiv-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>≡</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{2}\equiv-1</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="S3.SS1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{3}\equiv-b^{-1}\pmod{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>≡</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mspace style="width:0.949em;" width="0.949em"></mspace><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">mod</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{3}\equiv-b^{-1}\pmod{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>, while <math id="S3.SS1.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> has exactly one root.
If an odd <math id="S3.SS1.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell\mid b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell\mid b</annotation></semantics></math>, the symmetric calculation gives <math id="S3.SS1.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{2}\equiv 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>≡</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{2}\equiv 1</annotation></semantics></math>
and <math id="S3.SS1.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{1}\equiv a^{-1}\pmod{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>≡</mo><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mspace style="width:0.949em;" width="0.949em"></mspace><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">mod</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{1}\equiv a^{-1}\pmod{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>, with only <math id="S3.SS1.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{3}</annotation></semantics></math> having a root.
Since exactly one of <math id="S3.SS1.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a,b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a,b</annotation></semantics></math> is divisible by <math id="S3.SS1.p4.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math>, this also proves
<math id="S3.SS1.p4.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(3)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho(3)=1</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text">If <math id="S3.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\mid a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\mid a</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{3}</annotation></semantics></math> are always odd and <math id="S3.SS1.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> has one root
modulo <math id="S3.SS1.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>. If <math id="S3.SS1.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\mid b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\mid b</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS1.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> are always odd and <math id="S3.SS1.p5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{3}</annotation></semantics></math>
has one root. This proves (<a href="#S3.E18" title="In Lemma 3.1 (Primitive forms and local densities). ‣ 3.1. Cofactors and local densities ‣ 3. A uniform sieve over a thin cofactor strip ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a>).
The factors at <math id="S3.SS1.p5.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2,3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2,3</annotation></semantics></math> in (<a href="#S3.E19" title="In Lemma 3.1 (Primitive forms and local densities). ‣ 3.1. Cofactors and local densities ‣ 3. A uniform sieve over a thin cofactor strip ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">19</span></a>) have product <math id="S3.SS1.p5.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9</annotation></semantics></math>;
at <math id="S3.SS1.p5.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell&gt;3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell&gt;3</annotation></semantics></math> dividing <math id="S3.SS1.p5.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="ab" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">ab</annotation></semantics></math> the ratio to the generic factor is
<math id="S3.SS1.p5.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\ell-1)/(\ell-3)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\ell-1)/(\ell-3)</annotation></semantics></math>. At the remaining primes the generic factor is
<math id="S3.SS1.p5.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1+O(\ell^{-2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1+O(\ell^{-2})</annotation></semantics></math>, proving convergence.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2. </span>Uniform Selberg sieve</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use Richert’s classical upper-bound sieve in the form of
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>, Theorem 11.3, p. 135]</cite>; see also
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>, Chapters 4–5]</cite>. The point of using this formulation is that
its implied constant depends only on the fixed sieve parameters occurring
in <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\Omega_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\Omega_{1})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\Omega_{2}(\kappa))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\Omega_{2}(\kappa))</annotation></semantics></math> (and on the fixed exponent in the
condition <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z\leq X^{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>≤</mo><msup><mi>X</mi><mi>A</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z\leq X^{A}</annotation></semantics></math>), not on the coefficients of the linear forms.
We record the verification in our family because <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> grow with <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For real <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z&gt;2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z&gt;2</annotation></semantics></math> put <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P(z)=\prod_{\ell&lt;z}\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∏</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(z)=\prod_{\ell&lt;z}\ell</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="S3.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F(m)=L_{1}(m)L_{2}(m)L_{3}(m)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(m)=L_{1}(m)L_{2}(m)L_{3}(m)</annotation></semantics></math>. Extend <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> multiplicatively to
squarefree integers, with <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(1)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho(1)=1</annotation></semantics></math>. For every squarefree <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>, the
Chinese remainder theorem gives</p>
<table id="S3.E20" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(20)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E20.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="A_{d}:=\#\{1\leq m\leq M:d\mid F(m)\}=M\frac{\rho(d)}{d}+r_{d},\qquad|r_{d}|\leq\rho(d)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mi>#</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>F</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>M</mi><mfrac><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>d</mi></mfrac><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">|</mo><mo lspace="0.167em">≤</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{d}:=\#\{1\leq m\leq M:d\mid F(m)\}=M\frac{\rho(d)}{d}+r_{d},\qquad|r_{d}|\leq\rho(d).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">Indeed, there are exactly <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho(d)</annotation></semantics></math> relevant residue classes modulo <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>,
and each contains <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M/d+O(1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M/d+O(1)</annotation></semantics></math> integers in <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[1,M]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1,M]</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus Richert’s
remainder condition <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(R)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(R)</annotation></semantics></math>, namely <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|r_{d}|\leq\omega(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>ω</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|r_{d}|\leq\omega(d)</annotation></semantics></math> for squarefree <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>,
holds with his local-density function <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega(d)=\rho(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ω</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega(d)=\rho(d)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 3.2</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Uniform sifted-set bound)<span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For every fixed <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, uniformly for <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3&lt;z\leq M^{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>≤</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3&lt;z\leq M^{A}</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="S3.E21" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(21)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E21.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\#\{1\leq m\leq M:(F(m),P(z))=1\}\ll_{A}H(ab)\frac{M}{\log^{3}z}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>#</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>F</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><msub><mo>≪</mo><mi>A</mi></msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mfrac><mi>M</mi><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\#\{1\leq m\leq M:(F(m),P(z))=1\}\ll_{A}H(ab)\frac{M}{\log^{3}z},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where the implied constant is independent of <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a,b,M,z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a,b,M,z</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S3.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">We apply Richert’s Theorem 11.3 with <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X=M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X=M</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="S3.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega(\ell)=\rho(\ell)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ω</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega(\ell)=\rho(\ell)</annotation></semantics></math>. Let us check the hypotheses with constants
independent of <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">Richert’s condition <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\Omega_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\Omega_{1})</annotation></semantics></math> is</span></p>
<table id="S3.Ex37" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex37.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0\leq\frac{\omega(\ell)}{\ell}\leq 1-\frac{1}{A_{1}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>ω</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mfrac><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0\leq\frac{\omega(\ell)}{\ell}\leq 1-\frac{1}{A_{1}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p4.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text">By (<a href="#S3.E18" title="In Lemma 3.1 (Primitive forms and local densities). ‣ 3.1. Cofactors and local densities ‣ 3. <p id="S3.SS2.p6.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p6.2.1" class="ltx_text">Here Mertens’ product formula, together with the absolutely convergent
generic Euler product in (<a href="#S3.E19" title="In Lemma 3.1 (Primitive forms and local densities). ‣ 3.1. Cofactors and local densities ‣ 3. <math id="S3.SS2.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ll(\log z)^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≪</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ll(\log z)^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math>; extending the second product to all prime divisors
of <math id="S3.SS2.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="ab" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">ab</annotation></semantics></math> only increases it. This proves (<a href="#S3.E21" title="In Lemma 3.2 (Uniform sifted-set bound). ‣ 3.2. Uniform Selberg sieve ‣ 3. <div id="S3.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 3.3</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Fix <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/2&lt;\theta&lt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/2&lt;\theta&lt;1</annotation></semantics></math>. Uniformly for coprime <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a,b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a,b</annotation></semantics></math> satisfying
<math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6\mid ab" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6\mid ab</annotation></semantics></math> and (<a href="#S3.E13" title="In 3.1. Cofactors and local densities ‣ 3. A uniform sieve over a thin cofactor strip ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>), let <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\theta}(a,b;x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\theta}(a,b;x)</annotation></semantics></math> count integers
<math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0\leq m\leq M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0\leq m\leq M</annotation></semantics></math>, where</span></p>
<table id="S3.E22" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(22)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E22.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M=\left\lfloor\frac{x-n_{0}}{2ab}\right\rfloor," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>⌊</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>⌋</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M=\left\lfloor\frac{x-n_{0}}{2ab}\right\rfloor,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">for which all three values in (<a href="#S3.E15" title="In 3.1. Cofactors and local densities ‣ 3. A uniform sieve over a thin cofactor strip ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a>) are prime and
<math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{1}(m),L_{3}(m)&gt;x^{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>θ</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{1}(m),L_{3}(m)&gt;x^{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>. Then</span></p>
<table id="S3.E23" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E23.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="N_{\theta}(a,b;x)\ll_{\theta}H(ab)\frac{x}{ab\log^{3}x}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mo>≪</mo><mi>θ</mi></msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\theta}(a,b;x)\ll_{\theta}H(ab)\frac{x}{ab\log^{3}x}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>

</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.3" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S3.SS2.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text">Since <math id="S3.SS2.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{0}&lt;2ab" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{0}&lt;2ab</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="ab\leq x^{2-2\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">ab\leq x^{2-2\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="S3.E24" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(24)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E24.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="M=\frac{x}{2ab}+O(1)\asymp\frac{x}{ab},\qquad M\gg x^{2\theta-1},\qquad\log M\asymp_{\theta}\log x." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mi>O</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≍</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>≫</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mi>log</mi><mi>M</mi><msub><mo>≍</mo><mi>θ</mi></msub><mi>log</mi><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M=\frac{x}{2ab}+O(1)\asymp\frac{x}{ab},\qquad M\gg x^{2\theta-1},\qquad\log M\asymp_{\theta}\log x.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p7.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p7.2.1" class="ltx_text">All constants here are uniform in <math id="S3.SS2.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a,b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a,b</annotation></semantics></math> once <math id="S3.SS2.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> is sufficiently large
in terms of the fixed <math id="S3.SS2.p7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>. In particular <math id="S3.SS2.p7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math> uniformly.
The single endpoint <math id="S3.SS2.p7.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m=0</annotation></semantics></math> costs at most <math id="S3.SS2.p7.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text">Put</span></p>
<table id="S3.Ex44" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex44.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa=\frac{2\theta-1}{8},\qquad z=x^{\kappa}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>8</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>κ</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa=\frac{2\theta-1}{8},\qquad z=x^{\kappa}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p8.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p8.2.1" class="ltx_text">Then <math id="S3.SS2.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0&lt;\kappa&lt;\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0&lt;\kappa&lt;\theta</annotation></semantics></math>. Moreover (<a href="#S3.E24" title="In Proof. ‣ 3.2. Uniform Selberg sieve ‣ 3. A uniform sieve over a thin cofactor strip ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">24</span></a>) gives, uniformly
in <math id="S3.SS2.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a,b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a,b</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="S3.Ex45" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex45.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z^{4}=x^{(2\theta-1)/2}\leq M" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>z</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>≤</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z^{4}=x^{(2\theta-1)/2}\leq M</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p8.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p8.3.1" class="ltx_text">for all sufficiently large <math id="S3.SS2.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> depending only on <math id="S3.SS2.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>; hence
<math id="S3.SS2.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z\leq M^{1/4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>≤</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z\leq M^{1/4}</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus Lemma <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem2" title="Lemma 3.2 (Uniform sifted-set bound). ‣ 3.2. Uniform Selberg sieve ‣ 3. A uniform sieve over a thin cofactor strip ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a> applies with the fixed
choice <math id="S3.SS2.p8.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A=1/4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A=1/4</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p9.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p9.1.1" class="ltx_text">For a triple counted by <math id="S3.SS2.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\theta}(a,b;x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\theta}(a,b;x)</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S3.SS2.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="S3.SS2.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{1},L_{3}&gt;x^{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>θ</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{1},L_{3}&gt;x^{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>, while from (<a href="#S3.E15" title="In 3.1. Cofactors and local densities ‣ 3. A uniform sieve over a thin cofactor strip ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a>)</span></p>
<table id="S3.Ex46" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex46.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{2}=2aL_{1}-1&gt;x^{\theta}-1&gt;z" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>θ</mi></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{2}=2aL_{1}-1&gt;x^{\theta}-1&gt;z</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p9.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p9.2.1" class="ltx_text">for sufficiently large <math id="S3.SS2.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>. Since all three values are prime and exceed
<math id="S3.SS2.p9.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>, their product is coprime to <math id="S3.SS2.p9.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(z)</annotation></semantics></math>. Lemma <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem2" title="Lemma 3.2 (Uniform sifted-set bound). ‣ 3.2. Uniform Selberg sieve ‣ 3. A uniform sieve over a thin cofactor strip ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a> therefore
gives</span></p>
<table id="S3.Ex47" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex47.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="N_{\theta}(a,b;x)\ll_{\theta}1+H(ab)\frac{M}{\log^{3}z}\ll_{\theta}1+H(ab)\frac{x}{ab\log^{3}x}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mo>≪</mo><mi>θ</mi></msub><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mfrac><mi>M</mi><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow></mfrac><msub><mo>≪</mo><mi>θ</mi></msub><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\theta}(a,b;x)\ll_{\theta}1+H(ab)\frac{M}{\log^{3}z}\ll_{\theta}1+H(ab)\frac{x}{ab\log^{3}x}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p9.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p9.3.1" class="ltx_text">Finally, <math id="S3.SS2.p9.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H(ab)\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(ab)\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math> and (<a href="#S3.E24" title="In Proof. ‣ 3.2. Uniform Selberg sieve ‣ 3. A uniform sieve over a thin cofactor strip ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">24</span></a>) imply
<math id="S3.SS2.p9.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x/(ab\log^{3}x)\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>log</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x/(ab\log^{3}x)\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math> uniformly, so the endpoint term is absorbed.
This proves (<a href="#S3.E23" title="In Lemma 3.3. ‣ 3.2. Uniform Selberg sieve ‣ 3. A uniform sieve over a thin cofactor strip ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">23</span></a>).
∎</span></p>
</div>

</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3. </span>Harmonic summation over the strip</h3>

<div id="S3.Thmtheorem4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 3.4</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Mean and interval harmonic bounds)<span id="S3.Thmtheorem4.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">There is an absolute constant <math id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{H}</annotation></semantics></math> such that, for <math id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="S3.E25" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(25)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E25.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{H}(T):=\sum_{n\leq T}H(n)\leq C_{H}T,\qquad\sum_{n\leq T}\frac{H(n)}{n}\leq C_{H}(1+\log T)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">:=</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.000em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>n</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{H}(T):=\sum_{n\leq T}H(n)\leq C_{H}T,\qquad\sum_{n\leq T}\frac{H(n)}{n}\leq C_{H}(1+\log T).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For all real <math id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\leq U&lt;V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>U</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\leq U&lt;V</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="S3.E26" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(26)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E26.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{U&lt;n\leq V}\frac{H(n)}{n}\leq C_{H}\left(1+\log\frac{V}{U}\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>n</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>V</mi><mi>U</mi></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{U&lt;n\leq V}\frac{H(n)}{n}\leq C_{H}\left(1+\log\frac{V}{U}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<div id="S3.SS3.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> be multiplicative, with <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c(1)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c(1)=1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c(2)=c(3)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c(2)=c(3)=0</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="S3.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c(\ell)=2/(\ell-3)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c(\ell)=2/(\ell-3)</annotation></semantics></math> for primes <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell&gt;3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell&gt;3</annotation></semantics></math>, and
<math id="S3.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c(\ell^{k})=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c(\ell^{k})=0</annotation></semantics></math> for every prime <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math>.
Expanding the local factors gives <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H(n)=\sum_{d\mid n}c(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(n)=\sum_{d\mid n}c(d)</annotation></semantics></math>.
The coefficients are nonnegative, so</span></p>
<table id="S3.Ex48" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex48.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{H}(T)=\sum_{d\leq T}c(d)\left\lfloor\frac{T}{d}\right\rfloor\leq T\sum_{d\geq 1}\frac{c(d)}{d}=C_{H}T," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>⌊</mo><mfrac><mi>T</mi><mi>d</mi></mfrac><mo>⌋</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>d</mi></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{H}(T)=\sum_{d\leq T}c(d)\left\lfloor\frac{T}{d}\right\rfloor\leq T\sum_{d\geq 1}\frac{c(d)}{d}=C_{H}T,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text">where</span></p>
<table id="S3.Ex49" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex49.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{H}=\prod_{\ell&gt;3}\left(1+\frac{2}{\ell(\ell-3)}\right)&lt;\infty." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∏</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></munder><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{H}=\prod_{\ell&gt;3}\left(1+\frac{2}{\ell(\ell-3)}\right)&lt;\infty.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="S3.SS3.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text">For real endpoints partial summation is exactly</span></p>
<table id="S3.Ex50" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex50.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{U&lt;n\leq V}\frac{H(n)}{n}=\frac{A_{H}(V)}{V}-\frac{A_{H}(U)}{U}+\int_{U}^{V}\frac{A_{H}(t)}{t^{2}}\,dt." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>n</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>V</mi></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>U</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>U</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">+</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><mi>U</mi><mi>V</mi></msubsup><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{U&lt;n\leq V}\frac{H(n)}{n}=\frac{A_{H}(V)}{V}-\frac{A_{H}(U)}{U}+\int_{U}^{V}\frac{A_{H}(t)}{t^{2}}\,dt.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.p1.4.1" class="ltx_text">Discard the nonpositive term and use <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{H}(t)\leq C_{H}t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{H}(t)\leq C_{H}t</annotation></semantics></math> to obtain
(<a href="#S3.E26" title="In Lemma 3.4 (Mean and interval harmonic bounds). ‣ 3.3. Harmonic summation over the strip ‣ 3. A uniform sieve over a thin cofactor strip ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">26</span></a>). For the full harmonic sum, add <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H(1)=1=A_{H}(1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(1)=1=A_{H}(1)</annotation></semantics></math>
to the exact identity with <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U=1</annotation></semantics></math>. The negative boundary term cancels,
leaving <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{H}(T)/T+\int_{1}^{T}A_{H}(t)t^{-2}\,dt\leq C_{H}(1+\log T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">+</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>T</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{H}(T)/T+\int_{1}^{T}A_{H}(t)t^{-2}\,dt\leq C_{H}(1+\log T)</annotation></semantics></math>.
This includes <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=1</annotation></semantics></math> and does not enlarge <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{H}</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 3.5</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For fixed <math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/2&lt;\theta&lt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/2&lt;\theta&lt;1</annotation></semantics></math> and every <math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="S3.E27" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(27)</span></td>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E27.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\#\mathcal{N}_{\eta}(x)\ll_{\theta}\eta\frac{x}{\log x}+\frac{x}{\log^{2}x}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>#</mi><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mi>η</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mo>≪</mo><mi>θ</mi></msub><mi>η</mi><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\#\mathcal{N}_{\eta}(x)\ll_{\theta}\eta\frac{x}{\log x}+\frac{x}{\log^{2}x}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The implied constant and a sufficiently large threshold for <math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> are
independent of <math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
