<div id="S3.SS3.3" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Each <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in\mathcal{N}_{\eta}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mi>η</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\in\mathcal{N}_{\eta}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> determines a unique <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a,b)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a,b)</annotation></semantics></math> satisfying
(<a href="#S3.E13" title="In 3.1. Cofactors and local densities ‣ 3. A uniform sieve over a thin cofactor strip ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>), (<a href="#S3.E14" title="In 3.1. Cofactors and local densities ‣ 3. A uniform sieve over a thin cofactor strip ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a>), <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a,b)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a,b)=1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6\mid ab" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6\mid ab</annotation></semantics></math>.
Lemma <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem3" title="Lemma 3.3. ‣ 3.2. Uniform Selberg sieve ‣ 3. A uniform sieve over a thin cofactor strip ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>, applied before discarding the restrictions, gives</span></p>
<table id="S3.Ex51" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<p id="S3.SS3.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">For every positive integer pair, <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H(ab)\leq H(a)H(b)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(ab)\leq H(a)H(b)</annotation></semantics></math>; shared prime
factors can only increase the right side. With <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=x^{1-\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=x^{1-\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>,
we can now discard the arithmetic restrictions and the upper bound on
the inner variable <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>. Lemma <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem4" title="Lemma 3.4 (Mean and interval harmonic bounds). ‣ 3.3. Harmonic summation over the strip ‣ 3. A uniform sieve over a thin cofactor strip ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.4</span></a> gives</span></p>

the sieve). Multiplication by <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x/\log^{3}x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x/\log^{3}x</annotation></semantics></math> proves (<a href="#S3.E27" title="In Proposition 3.5. ‣ 3.3. ∎</span></p>

<div id="S3.Thmtheorem6" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 3.6</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Reflected thin-strip bound)<span id="S3.Thmtheorem6.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For fixed <math id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/2&lt;\theta&lt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/2&lt;\theta&lt;1</annotation></semantics></math> and every <math id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="S3.E28" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<p id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The implied constant and a sufficiently large threshold for <math id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> are
independent of <math id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>

<div id="S3.SS3.4" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S3.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}_{\eta}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>η</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\in\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}_{\eta}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> and write
<math id="S3.SS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q=Q(p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q=Q(p)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=R(p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=R(p)</annotation></semantics></math> and</span></p>
<table id="S3.Ex55" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex55.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p+1=2aq,\qquad p-1=2br,\qquad aq-br=1." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p+1=2aq,\qquad p-1=2br,\qquad aq-br=1.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">Here <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q&gt;r&gt;x^{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>θ</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q&gt;r&gt;x^{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>, so the box bounds (<a href="#S3.E13" title="In 3.1. Cofactors and local densities ‣ 3. A uniform sieve over a thin cofactor strip ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>), coprimality
<math id="S3.SS3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a,b)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a,b)=1</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6\mid ab" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6\mid ab</annotation></semantics></math> are unchanged. Moreover <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a&lt;b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a&lt;b</annotation></semantics></math>.
Indeed, if <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a\geq b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a\geq b</annotation></semantics></math>, then, since <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> are distinct odd primes,</span></p>
<table id="S3.Ex56" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex56.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1=aq-br=a(q-r)+(a-b)r\geq q-r\geq 2," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1=aq-br=a(q-r)+(a-b)r\geq q-r\geq 2,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.p3.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.p3.3.1" class="ltx_text">a contradiction. Also</span></p>
<table id="S3.Ex57" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex57.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{b}{a}=\frac{q}{r}\frac{p-1}{p+1}&lt;\frac{q}{r}\leq x^{\eta}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mi>b</mi><mi>a</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>q</mi><mi>r</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mfrac><mi>q</mi><mi>r</mi></mfrac><mo>≤</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>η</mi></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{b}{a}=\frac{q}{r}\frac{p-1}{p+1}&lt;\frac{q}{r}\leq x^{\eta},</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.p3.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.p3.4.1" class="ltx_text">so the cofactors lie in the reflected strip</span></p>

</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.p3.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.p3.5.1" class="ltx_text">For each such pair the same linear forms (<a href="#S3.E15" title="In 3.1. Cofactors and local densities ‣ 3. A uniform sieve over a thin cofactor strip ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a>) have prime
values <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q,p,r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q,p,r</annotation></semantics></math>, and Lemma <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem3" title="Lemma 3.3. ‣ 3.2. Uniform Selberg sieve ‣ 3. A uniform sieve over a thin cofactor strip ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a> applies without any change.
Consequently, after discarding <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a,b)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a,b)=1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6\mid ab" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6\mid ab</annotation></semantics></math> and using
<math id="S3.SS3.p3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H(ab)\leq H(a)H(b)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(ab)\leq H(a)H(b)</annotation></semantics></math>, with <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=x^{1-\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=x^{1-\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> we have</span></p>

<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4. </span>Completion of the argument</h2>

<div id="S4.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 4.1</span></span><span id="S4.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Square-root-breaking criterion)<span id="S4.Thmtheorem1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Fix <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/2&lt;\theta&lt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/2&lt;\theta&lt;1</annotation></semantics></math>. Suppose there is <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> such that,
for all sufficiently large <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="S4.E30" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(30)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E30.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\#\mathcal{A}_{\theta}(x)\geq\delta\frac{x}{\log x}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>#</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\#\mathcal{A}_{\theta}(x)\geq\delta\frac{x}{\log x}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Then <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="G(x)\gg_{\theta,\delta}x/\log x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mo>≫</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow></msub><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>log</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G(x)\gg_{\theta,\delta}x/\log x</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">For <math id="S4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p&gt;3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p&gt;3</annotation></semantics></math>, equality <math id="S4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q(p)=R(p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q(p)=R(p)</annotation></semantics></math> is impossible. A common largest
prime factor would divide <math id="S4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>, making both <math id="S4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p-1,p+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p-1,p+1</annotation></semantics></math> powers of <math id="S4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>.
If <math id="S4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p-1=2^{u}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>u</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p-1=2^{u}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p+1=2^{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>v</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p+1=2^{v}</annotation></semantics></math>, then
<math id="S4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2^{u}(2^{v-u}-1)=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>u</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>u</mi></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^{u}(2^{v-u}-1)=2</annotation></semantics></math>, forcing <math id="S4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u=1,v=2,p=3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u=1,v=2,p=3</annotation></semantics></math>.
Thus, up to a bounded endpoint exception,</span></p>
<table id="S4.Ex62" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<p id="S4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">For <math id="S4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p&gt;3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p&gt;3</annotation></semantics></math> equality <math id="S4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q(p)=R(p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q(p)=R(p)</annotation></semantics></math> is impossible, as observed in the
proof of Proposition <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem1" title="Proposition 4.1 (Square-root-breaking criterion). ‣ 4. Completion of the argument ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a>. Hence, up to a bounded
endpoint exception,</span></p>

<p id="S4.p2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p2.3.1" class="ltx_text">where <math id="S4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C^{\prime}_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi>θ</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C^{\prime}_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> is independent of <math id="S4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math>. Choosing <math id="S4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math> and then
<math id="S4.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> in the same order as in Proposition <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem1" title="Proposition 4.1 (Square-root-breaking criterion). ‣ 4. </div>
<div id="S4.4" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof of Theorem <a href="#S1.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 1.1. ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.1</span></a>.</h6>
<div id="S4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">Use Proposition <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem3" title="Proposition 2.3. ‣ 2.2. One-sided reservoirs for both shifts ‣ 2. Logarithmic estimates and far reverse orderings ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a> with
<math id="S4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta=11/20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta=11/20</annotation></semantics></math>. The bound <math id="S4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-\log(9/10)\leq 1/9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">−</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\log(9/10)\leq 1/9</annotation></semantics></math> gives
<math id="S4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta(11/20)&gt;1/4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta(11/20)&gt;1/4</annotation></semantics></math>. For <math id="S4.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s=1</annotation></semantics></math> the strict liminf margin yields
(<a href="#S4.E30" title="In Proposition 4.1 (Square-root-breaking criterion). ‣ 4. Completion of the argument ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">30</span></a>) with <math id="S4.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta=1/4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta=1/4</annotation></semantics></math> for all sufficiently large
<math id="S4.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, so Proposition <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem1" title="Proposition 4.1 (Square-root-breaking criterion). ‣ 4. Completion of the argument ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a> gives
<math id="S4.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G(x)\gg x/\log x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≫</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G(x)\gg x/\log x</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">For <math id="S4.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s=-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s=-1</annotation></semantics></math> the same proposition gives
(<a href="#S4.E32" title="In Proposition 4.2 (Reverse square-root-breaking criterion). ‣ 4. Completion of the argument ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">32</span></a>), again with <math id="S4.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta=1/4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta=1/4</annotation></semantics></math> for all
sufficiently large <math id="S4.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>. Proposition <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem2" title="Proposition 4.2 (Reverse square-root-breaking criterion). ‣ 4. Completion of the argument ‣ On the largest prime factors of 𝑝-1 and 𝑝+1" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>
therefore gives
<math id="S4.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{G}(x)\gg x/\log x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>G</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≫</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{G}(x)\gg x/\log x</annotation></semantics></math>.
The prime number theorem converts both estimates into the asserted
positive lower proportions.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
